newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee gains as banks sell dollars.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee gains as banks sell dollars.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee continued to firm as banks liquidated dollar positions in the face of dull demand and limited upside potential of the U.S. unit, dealers said.
At 0430 GMT the rupee was at 56.60 to the dollar after opening at 56.65. The rupee closed at 56.69 on Monday.
"We saw early selling of dollars, as some banks liquidated pluses," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
Slack local demand and the possibility that the dollar would end the year at current levels was probably prompting banks to sell the U.S. unit, he said.
The Central Bank brought down the dollar by .75 local cent, and fixed buying and selling rates at 56.0835 and 57.2165 rupees.
Overnight call money was at 15.75 percent after opening at 14.25 percent and rising early to 16.5 percent, dealers said.
"There is no reason for call money to rise just because there are a few borrowers, because the market is very liquid," said a Bank of Ceylon dealer.
